# 美国拟投资5000万美元严控AI芯片溯源，防止对华出口管制遭规避，巴拿马成首个试点

美国政府周三（8月12日）公布了一项最高达5000万美元的招标计划，旨在建立认证机制并加快人工智能（AI）产业所需关键零部件和矿产的贸易。据悉，这项全球性项目将首先与巴拿马开展试点，未来可能进一步推广至其他合作伙伴国家。按照设想，这一平台类似于电子元器件的“数字护照”，将对每批经巴拿马运河运输的货物进行原产地和运输路径认证，并为被认定为可靠的货物加快海关通关速度。在美国持续限制相关产品对华出口的背景下，该计划受到广泛关注。

发表时间： 13/08/2026 - 00:39

资料图片

该招标于上周启动，计划提供最高5000万美元的对外援助资金，相关资金将与美国国会协调落实。

近年来，美国持续限制最先进半导体向中国出口。这些芯片是训练人工智能模型所不可或缺的关键设备。与此同时，美国也试图防止第三国成为规避这些出口限制的中转渠道。

虽然招标文件始终没有直接点名中国，但文件将拟议中的平台描述为“战略竞争对手”物流体系的“替代方案”，并称后者可能被用于实施“经济胁迫”。

巴拿马运河承担着全球约5%的海运贸易，是美中关系紧张的一个焦点。2025年初，特朗普曾威胁要重新取得对巴拿马运河的控制权，并指责中国在这条战略性航道上占据主导地位。此后，巴拿马司法部门撤销了由香港企业集团长江和记实业旗下子公司运营的运河两座港口的特许经营权，引发中国方面加强对巴拿马船只的管控。两国关系于今年7月出现缓和迹象，双方续签了一项海运协议。

# Fashion industry leverages AI to optimize inventory management

12 August 2026 Consultancy-me.com 3 min. read

The traditional model of planning fashion sales months in advance is undergoing a major shift, according to a new insight paper from LOGIC Consulting. With AI, companies are better equipped to cut back on losses.

Retailers have long struggled with committing inventory before knowing actual consumer demand, leading to sub-optimized inventory levels and financial impacts. Globally, inventory distortion from overstocking and out-of-stock items costs the retail industry nearly $1.73 trillion annually, despite recent improvements of $172 billion. [...] To solve this mismatch, fashion brands are turning to AI to adjust stock levels, personalize customer experiences, and protect profit margins.

## A shift toward real-time planning

Rather than relying purely on pre-season guesswork, retailers use AI to analyze customer browsing, store traffic, and sales data as trends happen. For example, shoe retailer FLO implemented an AI-powered demand engine to track stock levels across its store network. By shifting stock to locations with higher demand, the company achieved a 12% reduction in lost sales and boosted total revenue by 4.7%. [...] Similarly, apparel company LPP uses AI to monitor social media signals, cutting its product design timeline down from up to 12 months to roughly six to 12 weeks. This rapid adjustment model allows brands to launch popular trends without committing heavy capital up front.

## Smarter marketing and personalization

AI tools are also transforming how companies market products and engage online shoppers. E-commerce platform Zalando reduced its marketing image creation timeline from six to eight weeks down to three to four days, cutting associated costs by 90% with AI-generated visuals.

# Megadeals took 87.5% of US venture dollars, and the rest of the market is priced by vintage

Rounds of $100m or more took 87.5% of every US venture dollar in the first half. The sharper number is what happened to everyone who last raised in 2021.

PitchBook published its Q2 US VC Valuations report on 10 August. Megadeals took 87.5% of the dollars deployed in the first half of 2026. PitchBook defines those as rounds of $100m or more. AI is the primary driver of that concentration, though the figure describes deal size rather than sector. [...] The AI premium is real and it shows up in two separate measures. AI companies posted a median valuation step-up of 2.2x this year against 1.6x for non-AI. Separately, AI pre-money valuations run roughly double non-AI at Series A. By Series D and later that comparison reaches 6.6x.

## The velocity number is the one to keep

Emily Zheng, a senior research analyst at PitchBook, pointed Fortune at the late-stage figure. Median velocity of value creation at Series D and beyond was $108.9m in 2025. This year it reached $1,028m. That is close to a tenfold rise in twelve months. [...] “Top AI companies like Anthropic are driving this growth, as its valuation grew 5.3x in just eight months,” Zheng said. Our own reporting has tracked that climb. Median AI pre-money valuation at Series D and later now sits at $3.95bn.

## The market is pricing the vintage, not the business

Here is the finding that deserved the headline. On the secondary platform Forge, companies whose last primary round was in 2026 trade at no discount at all. For 2025 the median discount is 4.7%.

Then it falls off a cliff. Companies that last raised in 2021 trade at a median discount of 59.1%. For 2022 it is 54.1%. Two businesses with the same revenue get different prices. The only difference is the year on their last term sheet.

# Learning contact representations in real-world clutter for universal robotic grasping

 Xianli Wang 
  ORCID: orcid.org/0000-0002-6537-91091,
 Lap Mou Tam1 &
 Qingsong Xu 
  ORCID: orcid.org/0000-0002-1700-322X1

Nature Machine Intelligence
(2026) Cite this article

Save article

## Abstract [...] A long-standing goal in robotics is to create general-purpose agents that can learn foundational skills applicable across diverse hardware and environments. In manipulation, this is hindered by a fundamental mismatch: deep learning policies are data-efficient but hardware-specific, whereas analytical planners are hardware-agnostic but fail under perceptual uncertainty. Here we introduce SpaHybGen, a framework that unifies their strengths through learned, universal contact representations. We first train a neural network to infer spatial contact features—a hardware-agnostic representation of potential grasp points—directly from noisy depth observations. These features then guide a differentiable optimizer that computes stable grasps for articulated hand models. This hybrid design enables [...] for articulated hand models. This hybrid design enables zero-shot generalization: our system, trained once, successfully empowered seven distinct robotic hands (from two to five fingers) without any hardware-specific retraining, achieving grasping success rates of 94.3%–98.0% in semi-cluttered scenes. It further enabled dynamic grasping at 20 Hz in dense clutter and multi-hand coordination for complex tasks. By decoupling perception from action through a shared contact interface, we provide a pathway towards reusable and adaptable manipulation intelligence, a key step for general-purpose robotics. Our code and models are open-sourced to support this vision.

## Abstract [...] Diagnosis of concussion has been hampered by its subtle and late symptoms, the reliance on subjective judgment, and the lack of real-time multimodal data integration. The developed computational models are generally black boxes and lack the robustness required for safety-critical scenarios. We introduce a symmetry-aware, multiscale, explainable, hybrid deep learning framework for early prediction of concussion risk. The system effectively combines kinematic sensor data, EEG, contextual information, and synchronized video using separate modality-specific feature extractors and a multimodal fusion layer that utilizes attention-based multimodality fusion. The framework is evaluated using subject-independent 5-fold cross-validation to evaluate its generalizability. The proposed framework [...] to evaluate its generalizability. The proposed framework incorporates explainability with SHAP value analysis and attention visualizations. The proposed system achieves an accuracy of 0.91, a macro F1-score of 0.90, and an AUC of 0.95, outperforming baselines that rely on single modalities and traditional multimodal integration. High concussion risk events are recalled with an F1-score of 0.89, and moderate concussion events are predicted with an F1-score of 0.87 to capture subtle injury characteristics. # Hong Kong-based startup Weina AI publishes paper in Nature, becoming the fourth global data-driven AI company featured in a major journal.

Summary [...] Weina AI, a Hong Kong-based startup, has become the first Chinese and fourth globally data-driven AI company to publish in a main Nature journal. The paper, titled “AI-Assisted Decision-Making in Kidney Cancer Surgery,” appears in Nature Communications. Led by Professor Liu Qifeng, the team previously built Hong Kong’s first 1,000-H800 SuperPod AI cluster and trained China’s third trillion-parameter model. The RDPM model integrates 3D imaging and clinical data to predict kidney failure risk, supporting surgical decision-making. Weina AI is focused on enhancing AI’s ability to pose questions and generate reasoning data for autonomous learning. This advancement could influence event-driven trading strategies in the crypto market, particularly for investors focused on value investing in [...] Weina Intelligence has successfully passed a public test of AI prediction in the most unforgiving scenario—healthcare. This points to the other side of AI prediction that Liu Qifeng will discuss next: prediction is, in fact, a fundamental mechanism of large models—generating answers by predicting the next token makes them inherently “good at answering.” But Weina Intelligence’s focus goes further—to make AI not just good at answering, but also good at asking. For AI to truly possess “knowledge,” it must not only be able to absorb information, but also be able to generate insightful questions.

# Learning contact representations in real-world clutter for universal robotic grasping

 Xianli Wang 
  ORCID: orcid.org/0000-0002-6537-91091,
 Lap Mou Tam1 &
 Qingsong Xu 
  ORCID: orcid.org/0000-0002-1700-322X1

Nature Machine Intelligence
(2026) Cite this article

Save article

## Abstract [...] A long-standing goal in robotics is to create general-purpose agents that can learn foundational skills applicable across diverse hardware and environments. In manipulation, this is hindered by a fundamental mismatch: deep learning policies are data-efficient but hardware-specific, whereas analytical planners are hardware-agnostic but fail under perceptual uncertainty. Here we introduce SpaHybGen, a framework that unifies their strengths through learned, universal contact representations. We first train a neural network to infer spatial contact features—a hardware-agnostic representation of potential grasp points—directly from noisy depth observations. These features then guide a differentiable optimizer that computes stable grasps for articulated hand models. This hybrid design enables [...] for articulated hand models. This hybrid design enables zero-shot generalization: our system, trained once, successfully empowered seven distinct robotic hands (from two to five fingers) without any hardware-specific retraining, achieving grasping success rates of 94.3%–98.0% in semi-cluttered scenes. It further enabled dynamic grasping at 20 Hz in dense clutter and multi-hand coordination for complex tasks. By decoupling perception from action through a shared contact interface, we provide a pathway towards reusable and adaptable manipulation intelligence, a key step for general-purpose robotics. Our code and models are open-sourced to support this vision.

items.title: Zuckerberg wants Washington to accept AI distillation - Politico
items.summary: Zuckerberg’s defense of distillation supports his essay’s larger argument for the U.S. to more aggre
items.content:
Zuckerberg’s defense of distillation supports his essay’s larger argument for the U.S. to more aggressively cultivate open-source AI. The conventional wisdom is that while America’s most advanced closed models are the most capable in the world, China has a leg up in the open-source ecosystem. As the White House considers restrictions on China’s AI, Zuckerberg has made a plea for continued access to open models, which can often be legitimately distilled.

He writes in the Monday post, “Restricting people and companies from using the leading open source models — wherever they come from — will reduce the quality of AI accessible to them, and centralize AI rather than putting more power in people’s hands.”

items.title: As AI safety concerns mount, three pioneers make the case for staying open - TechCrunch
items.summary: Yet accepting reality didn’t mean ignoring the risks. Hinton’s position was clear: AI would continue
items.content:
Yet accepting reality didn’t mean ignoring the risks. Hinton’s position was clear: AI would continue to advance, and he thought that was largely a good thing. He said it would boost productivity and improve education and healthcare. “Worrying about the possible bad effects of AI and the things that intelligent beings might do when they’re smarter than us. I don’t think that’s unfair. I think it is unfair to label anybody who thinks like that as a fear-monger,” Hinton added. [...] She also highlighted collaborations between public and private institutions, such as the Human Genome Project. The resulting knowledge became a platform that others could build on, she said, allowing pharmaceutical companies to profit, scientists to advance their work and society to benefit.

“So I think we have to use [AI] as that kind of infrastructure,” Li said. “We need some levels of openness, both in scientific discovery, in education, in global partnership, as well as lucrative business models for entrepreneurs. But we also will accept closed-source systems. This debate, especially at the sweeping level of ‘we can only tolerate one,’ is a false debate. We need to get to a level of nuance.” [...] For the three speakers, the core concern was allowing a handful of major AI companies to control the pace of progress. When a few companies control access to a technology, as Apple and Google do with mobile operating systems, innovation can slow and the companies that control the platforms can influence what gets built on them.

Andrew Ng said that he worried about a similar dynamic emerging in AI. “I don’t want there to be gatekeepers,” Ng said. “That limits how all of us can access AI.”

Companies have an incentive to protect their competitive advantages, including by influencing the rules that govern the industry. That could create a dynamic where only the largest, best-capitalized firms with the resources to build the most advanced AI systems.

What if you didn’t have to dig through your inbox to schedule a follow-up doctor’s appointment or type on a tiny keyboard to send emails on your way to work?

That’s the future Google and other tech giants predict, with AI agents soon handling tasks on our phones without constant prompting, potentially freeing us up to do other things.

The company’s newest Pixel smartphones, announced Wednesday, carry features aimed in that direction.A new light on the Pixel 11 Pro’s back will show when Gemini processes a command, and a new Android feature later this year called Halo will show an AI agent’s progress on a given task. [...] But growing public unease over the technology’s social and economic impacts underscore the risks for AI’s future. And the tech is still far from being able to carry out the kind of future Samat outlined to CNN.

Still, Google is banking on that vision.

“I see a lot of folks, including myself, that are heads down in their phones, trying to get a lot of things done,” he said. “And if you can give people that time back, five minutes a day, 10 minutes a day, 30 minutes a day, think what you can do with that.”

## Using your phone less

The days of switching between apps to complete a task could be numbered. [...] “It’s just a word that has come to mean a lot of things,” Samat said referring to AI. “Instead of talking about the tech, I think one of the things that’s been much more of a focus for us is… ‘How does it actually help you?’”
